gaps.sentence: Our team ___ the championship twice in the last five years.
gaps.hint: in the last five years up to now
gaps.explanation: 'In the last five years' is a period up to the present, so the present perfect fits: has won.

gaps.sentence: As soon as the plane landed, everyone ___ their phones.
gaps.hint: as soon as links two past actions
gaps.explanation: 'As soon as' links two sequential completed actions, so the past simple is used: switched on.

gaps.sentence: Look at those clouds — it ___ any minute now.
gaps.explanation: A prediction based on present evidence uses 'be going to': is going to rain.

gaps.sentence: I ___ the doctor's on Tuesday; I made the appointment yesterday.
gaps.hint: a fixed appointment arranged for the future
gaps.explanation: A personal arrangement already made takes the present continuous: am going.

gaps.sentence: She ___ me yesterday to say she had arrived safely.
gaps.hint: yesterday fixes a finished past action
gaps.explanation: 'Yesterday' is a finished past time, so the past simple is used: phoned.

gaps.sentence: This time next week I ___ on a beach in Portugal, with my phone switched off.
gaps.hint: this time next week means in progress
gaps.explanation: 'This time next week' points to an action in progress at a future moment, so the future continuous fits: will be lying.

gaps.sentence: By next April, we ___ here for ten years.
gaps.hint: duration leading up to a future point
gaps.explanation: A duration leading up to a future point takes the future perfect continuous: will have been living.

gaps.sentence: The committee ___ for three hours by the time anyone mentioned the budget.
gaps.hint: duration up to a past point
gaps.explanation: 'By the time + past' requires the past perfect continuous for the ongoing activity.
